comments.body:
IMPLEMENTED — commit 90f3380347 on branch fix/043f-84aa-infra (NOT pushed to Gerrit per instruction).

SHAPE OF THE FIX: one idempotent documented path. `scripts/install-gerrit-hook.sh` +
`make hooks` (which `make install` already calls), and the bare curl is removed from both
AGENTS.md and CONTRIBUTING.md. Chosen over 'make the curl smarter' because `make hooks`
already owns the chained pre-commit/Gerrit arrangement and already VERIFIES the Change-Id
chain survived — it only lacked the ability to INSTALL the stamper, so it warned and then
handed the user a curl. Folding the install in removes the second path entirely.

The script is:
* cwd-independent — resolves `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` and absolutises it, so it
  behaves identically from the main checkout, a subdirectory, or a linked worktree.
* non-destructive — when a pre-commit wrapper owns the `commit-msg` slot it installs to
  `commit-msg.legacy` (the slot pre-commit's migration chain runs), never over the wrapper.
* idempotent — existing Change-Id stamping in either slot is a no-op exit 0. Required,
  because `make hooks` runs on every `make install`.
* loud on the unsafe case (AC4) — a `commit-msg` hook that is neither a pre-commit wrapper
  nor a Change-Id stamper is REFUSED with a nonzero exit and a message, not overwritten.
* payload-validating — refuses to install a fetched file that contains no Change-Id logic
  (an HTML error page or a truncated download would otherwise become an executable hook).
* offline-testable — `REBAR_GERRIT_HOOK_SOURCE` installs from a local file, which is how the
  test suite exercises it hermetically.

EVIDENCE, both directions:
* RED (defect pinned): test_the_old_documented_path_targets_the_shared_precommit_slot proves
  `git rev-parse --git-path hooks/commit-msg` from a LINKED worktree resolves to the MAIN
  checkout's shared hook, and then performs that write to show the pre-commit wrapper is
  destroyed. RED for the docs half was 3 real offenders: AGENTS.md:224, CONTRIBUTING.md:55,
  CONTRIBUTING.md:426.
* MUTATION (fix pinned): changing the installer's `target=\$legacy` to `target=\$wrapper`
  makes 2 of 5 tests FAIL — 'the installer overwrote the shared pre-commit wrapper'. So the
  tests discriminate the slot choice, not merely that a file appeared.
* END-TO-END on the real host: `make hooks` from the worktree exits 0, prints
  'Gerrit Change-Id stamping already installed (…/commit-msg.legacy, chained by pre-commit)',
  and commit-msg.legacy's md5 is UNCHANGED (88bebbbf62ce56b94f4f4c7139edc845) before and
  after. Both real commits on this branch were stamped through that chain.

AUDIT of the other .claude/settings.json hook entries for the same relative-path defect
(ticket c6f6 — NOT fixed here, as instructed): the project settings file has exactly ONE hook
entry, PreToolUse/Bash -> 'scripts/hooks/serena_grep_reminder.py', and it IS relative, so it
is the single instance of c6f6 in the project file. There is no .claude/settings.local.json.
The user-global ~/.claude/settings.json hooks ('rtk hook claude', 'terminal-notifier …') are
PATH-resolved commands, not relative file paths, so they are not affected. Nothing in this
change touches that entry.

INCIDENTAL OBSERVATION, not a regression and not fixed here: `pre-commit install` (which
`make hooks` runs) re-templates the SHARED commit-msg/pre-commit wrappers with an absolute
INSTALL_PYTHON pointing at whichever worktree's venv ran it last. Before this session's run
the shared wrapper pointed at /Users/joeoakhart/fix/b718-9ac2-caplog/.venv. It degrades
gracefully (the wrapper falls back to `command -v pre-commit`), but it means `make hooks`
is inherently host-wide for the wrapper too. Same shared-hooks-dir root as this ticket.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

The `commit-msg` hook install command documented in AGENTS.md and CONTRIBUTING.md is WORKTREE-UNSAFE.
It silently clobbers the shared, pre-commit-managed hook for EVERY worktree, and the damage is
invisible until a Gerrit push is rejected for a missing `Change-Id`.

The documented command:

    curl -sLo "$(git rev-parse --git-path hooks/commit-msg)" https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/tools/hooks/commit-msg && chmod +x "$(git rev-parse --git-path hooks/commit-msg)"

`git rev-parse --git-path hooks/commit-msg` run from inside a linked worktree does NOT resolve to that
worktree — hooks live in the shared common dir, so it resolves to `/…/rebar/.git/hooks/commit-msg`.
The curl therefore OVERWRITES the pre-commit wrapper in the main checkout.

## Why the damage is worse than one broken worktree

`.pre-commit-config.yaml:16-19` documents the intended arrangement explicitly: pre-commit installs in
MIGRATION mode, preserving Gerrit's hook as `commit-msg.legacy` and running BOTH, and warns "never
install with `-f`/`--overwrite`, which would drop the Change-Id stamp and break every push to Gerrit."
The curl achieves exactly that forbidden state by a different route — it replaces the wrapper rather
than chaining to it, so the pre-commit `commit-msg` gate (the 50/72 message rule) stops running, and
once someone later reinstalls pre-commit over it the Gerrit stamper is the half that disappears.

Either way the failure is SILENT at commit time and only surfaces at `git push gerrit`, potentially
many commits later, in a DIFFERENT worktree than the one that ran the curl.

## Evidence: this is not hypothetical, it happened twice in one session

Two independent agents, working different tickets in different worktrees, each ran the documented
command and each clobbered `/Users/joeoakhart/rebar/.git/hooks/commit-msg`. Both noticed and repaired
it with `make hooks`, and the repaired state was verified both times:

    commit-msg          641 bytes   pre-commit wrapper
    commit-msg.legacy  3127 bytes   Gerrit stamper, contains the Change-Id logic

They noticed because they were told to report side effects. An agent not told to look would have left
the repo with Change-Id stamping broken for every worktree on the host.

## Approach

Make the documented command worktree-correct and non-destructive. Options to weigh, not yet decided:

- Resolve the shared hooks dir deliberately and refuse to overwrite a pre-commit wrapper, instructing
  the user to run `make hooks` instead.
- Fold the Gerrit hook install into `make hooks` so there is ONE documented way to get both hooks and
  it is idempotent — this is the likely right answer, since `make hooks` already owns the chained
  arrangement.
- Have the command write `commit-msg.legacy` directly when a pre-commit wrapper is present.

Whichever is chosen, the docs in AGENTS.md and CONTRIBUTING.md must stop telling contributors to curl
over `--git-path hooks/commit-msg`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Running the documented install from inside a linked worktree leaves BOTH hooks functional: the
      pre-commit wrapper and the Gerrit Change-Id stamper.
- [ ] A test or scripted check asserts that after the documented install, a commit made in a worktree
      receives a `Change-Id` AND is subject to the pre-commit `commit-msg` gate.
- [ ] AGENTS.md and CONTRIBUTING.md no longer instruct a bare curl over
      `$(git rev-parse --git-path hooks/commit-msg)`.
- [ ] The failure mode is made loud rather than silent: attempting the unsafe overwrite warns or
      refuses instead of succeeding quietly.
- [ ] make lint and make typecheck pass by exit code; the default selection is green.
compiled_state.title: The documented commit-msg hook install is worktree-unsafe and silently clobbers Change-Id stamping for every worktree
